summary.text: Scott Sharp is a Republican state representative who has represented Kentucky House of Representatives District 100 since 2021 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A U.S. Army veteran and former special agent with the Criminal Investigation Command, he sits on the House Veterans, Military Affairs, and Public Protection Committee.

paragraphs.text: Scott Sharp served in the U.S. Army, and he earned an M.S. in organizational psychology from St. Joseph University and an M.A. in management from Webster University.
His career experience includes working as a special agent with the Criminal Investigation Command and teaching at Ohio University Southern Campus.

He lost a general election for the Kentucky State Senate in District 18 in 2018, and he won the House District 100 seat in 2020, taking office on January 1, 2021, as the successor to Terri Branham Clark.
For 2025-2026 he was assigned to the Economic Development and Workforce Investment, Health and Family Services, and Veterans, Military Affairs, and Public Protection committees.
The Republican primary for his seat on May 19, 2026, was canceled.
